editorial:
Ten years after a deadly virus wiped out most of humanity, a group of survivors in San Francisco tries to rebuild while Caesar leads a growing ape community in the nearby woods. When the two sides meet, trust is fragile and fear runs high. You get pulled into a tense story where both humans and apes just want to survive, but old wounds and bad choices keep pushing them toward war. The movie feels grounded and emotional, with stunning motion-capture performances that make the apes feel real.

The action is intense and well-shot, and the pacing keeps you invested without rushing. Andy Serkis as Caesar is incredible, and the supporting cast holds up well. The downside is that some human characters feel a bit thin, and the story can feel heavy at times. If you enjoy smart sci-fi with heart and big set pieces, this is for you. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture.
endingExplained: In the final act, Koba betrays Caesar and leads an attack on the human survivors, taking over the ape colony. Caesar recovers and confronts Koba on a collapsing tower. After a brutal fight, Caesar lets Koba fall to his death, declaring he is not an ape. Caesar then prepares his people for war as the humans call for military backup. The twist is that peace was never possible, and both sides are now locked into conflict.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves smart sci-fi with heart and big set pieces.
